reason: This passage from 1 Chronicles 21 primarily demonstrates God's severe judgment and punishment of Israel rather than His desire for their wellbeing. While the text does show eventual mercy (God stops the plague when David repents and accepts his sacrifice), the dominant narrative arc involves: (1) God being displeased with David's census ('וַיֵּרַע בְּעֵינֵי הָאֱלֹהִים'), (2) God offering three terrible punishments, (3) God sending pestilence that kills 70,000 innocent Israelites ('וַיִּפֹּל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שִׁבְעִים אֶלֶף אִישׁ'), and (4) an angel of destruction hovering over Jerusalem with a drawn sword. Although God's mercy is shown at the end ('וַיִּנָּחֶם עַל־ הָרָעָה'), the overwhelming focus of this text is on punishment, not on Yahweh wanting the people to be well. The passage illustrates divine judgment and conditional mercy rather than an inherent desire for the people's welfare.
